date_note: SA Home Loans says it detected the access on 13 November; TechCentral's article is dated 25 November.
title: SA Home Loans says an unknown party accessed some of its systems, including one used for collections
summary: SA Home Loans says an unknown third party gained unauthorised access to some of its systems, including one used for collections, detected on 13 November. It says the information may include customers' names, bank account numbers and branch codes plus some payment details. It says it has no evidence that home loan accounts were accessed or altered, and does not know the threat actor's identity. It has notified the Information Regulator, per TechCentral.
plain: SA Home Loans says an unknown party got into some of its systems, and customers' names, bank account numbers and branch codes may be affected. It says it has no evidence that loan accounts were accessed or changed.
exec: SA Home Loans reports unauthorised access to systems including collections, with customer names and bank details possibly involved; it has told the Information Regulator and brought in forensic specialists.
action: As SA Home Loans advises, review bank statements and challenge debit orders you do not recognise, and be wary of phishing messages claiming to be from SAHL or your bank.

validation.note: Only TechCentral, relaying SAHL's statement, was read; SAHL's own notice was not found.
